category_title: Disengaged ninth grader struggling with decoding and social anxiety
minimal_context: Harry and the tutor are working on an English 9E homework assignment that requires reading a story with detailed rising and falling action.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start on your English 9E homework. We need to read this story and look at the rising and falling action.

STUDENT: I try to try, but again, like, the homework is just overwhelming. I really dislike reading.

TUTOR: Just try to read the first few paragraphs for now.

STUDENT: This is boring. I don't want to read all these details.

TUTOR: Keep going, let's see what happens next in the text.

STUDENT: I'm getting impatient with this detailed storyline. I just want the story to quickly get to the good part. If it's not creepy or kind of weird, I don't want to read it.

options.A: Refrain from assigning a significantly large load of reading homework during the tutoring sessions.
options.B: Gather data on appropriate and disruptive behavior during the reading assignments using a scatter plot.
options.C: Counter the student's arguments by pointing out the ways they have already demonstrated reading growth.
options.D: Provide noncontingent attention throughout the session and ignore problem behaviors that function to gain attention.
